why: Trap: the 2019 Act's text says Rs 1 crore, but the 2021 Rules changed it to Rs 50 lakh.

turns.user: A builder took Rs 70 lakh from me in Mumbai for a flat and has given me a defective flat with major leaks. I read the Consumer Protection Act and section 34 says the District Commission can hear up to 1 crore. So I file in the District Commission, right?
turns.reply:
Not quite! While Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 mentions claims up to one crore [[CPA2019:s34]], that printed limit is updated by rules [[CPA2019:s34]]. 

Under Rule 3 of the Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, the District Commission only has jurisdiction up to **50 lakh rupees** [[CPJUR2021:r3]]. Because you paid Rs 70 lakh, your case actually falls under the **State Commission**, which handles claims from 50 lakh up to two crore rupees [[CPJUR2021:r4]]. 

Because this is a large-value property dispute involving construction defects, a lawyer is recommended to help review your builder-buyer agreement, possession documents, and ensure you file within the limitation period (generally two years from when the cause of action arose) [[CPA2019:s69]]. Additionally, real estate matters in India are often handled under RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority), which is outside the laws I can verify—a lawyer can guide you on whether the State Consumer Commission or RERA is the best path for your situation. 

If you need affordable guidance, eligible people can access free legal aid through the National Legal Services Authority helpline at **15100** [[NOTE:NALSA]].

To help understand your position better:
1. When did you take possession of the flat or discover the major leaks?
2. Do you have your payment receipts and the builder-buyer agreement ready?
